hypothesis: The current ACCDB solve selects HOT_MOD1 whenever caseMode.thermal is true. Hexagon CAESAR II authority states that FBDR is the only piping code that uses hot modulus in the flexibility analysis; B31.3 therefore uses the cold elastic modulus for flexibility even when HOT_MOD1 is populated. BM4_NL is on the qualified B31.3/B31J path. Replacing only the L20 flexibility modulus selection with the ACCDB MODULUS field should remove a systematic thermal-case stiffness error while leaving accepted I015 L19 mechanics exactly invariant.

authoritySources.authorityStatement: FBDR is the only piping code in CAESAR II which uses the hot modulus in the flexibility analysis.

authoritySources.document: CAESAR II User's Guide - Elastic Properties
authoritySources.authorityStatement: EH1 through EH9 are populated hot elastic moduli for operating conditions; their presence in input is not itself authority to use them in B31.3 flexibility.
